name: Shackleton–de Gerlache Connecting Ridge
summary: The most persistently sunlit terrain near the lunar south pole (~88% of the time at 2 m height in LOLA models) and adjacent to Shackleton/de Gerlache PSR cold traps; a 2022 Artemis III candidate region and the archetype polar base site for power + ice access.
missions: Artemis III (2022 candidate region, dropped in Oct 2024 refinement)

env.water_vapor_note: No atmosphere (surface-bounded exosphere). Water ice cold-trapped in adjacent PSRs (Shackleton floor, de Gerlache) below ~110 K.
env.uv_note: Unfiltered solar UV including UVC; Sun is only ~1.5-2 deg above the horizon so irradiance on horizontal surfaces is tiny, but vertical/sun-facing surfaces receive full 1 AU flux. DNA-weighted factor vs Earth surface is for normal incidence.
env.terrain: Narrow highland ridge (Shackleton rim to de Gerlache rim), slopes 5-15 deg, flanked by permanently shadowed crater floors.
env.dust: Fine, electrostatically charged, abrasive highland regolith; no wind.

sources.label: LPI 2020: Shackleton–de Gerlache ridge 88% illumination at 2 m (Mazarico et al. 2011 data)
JGR Planets 2025: Artemis CLR landing-site coordinates (CR sites ~-89.5, -137)
Chang'e-4 LND lunar surface dose 1369 uSv/day
Paige et al. 2010 Diviner cold traps

name: de Gerlache Rim 2 (Artemis III candidate)
summary: Rim of de Gerlache crater near the Shackleton–de Gerlache ridge; high-elevation, well-lit terrain next to the large de Gerlache PSR. One of NASA's nine refined Artemis III regions (Oct 2024).

env.water_vapor_note: No atmosphere; de Gerlache crater floor is a PSR cold trap (<110 K) adjacent to the rim.
env.uv_note: Unfiltered solar UV at grazing incidence (sun <= ~3.4 deg).
env.terrain: Crater rim highlands with 5-15 deg slopes; ~30 km2 meets HLS landing constraints (~7.5% of region).
env.dust: Fine, charged, abrasive highland regolith.

sources.label: NASA Oct 2024: refined Artemis III landing regions
JGR Planets 2025: candidate landing sites in Artemis CLRs (dGR2 sites -88.0 to -88.4, -62 to -75)

name: Malapert Massif (Mons Malapert)
summary: A ~5 km-high massif on the nearside limb with exceptional, near-continuous Earth visibility (direct-to-Earth comms) plus good illumination; Artemis III candidate.

env.water_vapor_note: No atmosphere; small PSRs on massif flanks and Haworth/Shoemaker cold traps nearby.
env.uv_note: Unfiltered solar UV; sun max ~5.5 deg elevation.
env.terrain: Steep massif; only ~7 km2 (1.6%) meets HLS landing constraints. Summit/rim plateaus are the landing targets.
env.dust: Fine, charged highland regolith; massif ejecta/basin material (South Pole–Aitken related).

sources.label: NASA Oct 2024: refined Artemis III landing regions

name: Mons Mouton (Leibnitz Beta)
summary: Large flat-topped massif (formerly Leibnitz Beta) with extensive illuminated plateau and nearby PSRs; Artemis III candidate and VIPER's former target area.
missions: Intuitive Machines IM-2 Athena (landed on plateau near Mons Mouton, Mar 2025)

env.water_vapor_note: No atmosphere; accessible PSRs <110 K identified at some MMO candidate sites.
env.uv_note: Unfiltered solar UV; sun max ~6 deg elevation.
env.terrain: Massif summit and flanks; ~21 km2 (8%) meets HLS constraints.
env.dust: Fine, charged highland regolith.

summary: By far the largest Artemis III candidate region, a relatively flat plateau with ~565 km2 meeting landing constraints and several accessible cold PSRs.

env.water_vapor_note: No atmosphere; accessible PSRs <110 K at several candidate sites.
env.uv_note: Unfiltered solar UV; sun max ~7 deg elevation.
env.terrain: Broad plateau, gentle slopes (<8 deg over large areas).
env.dust: Fine, charged highland regolith.

name: Nobile Rim 1 & 2
summary: Rim of Nobile crater (a large PSR cold trap). Merges Nobile Rim 1 (~-85.2, 37.2) and Nobile Rim 2 (~-83.9, 58.3), both Artemis III candidates; NR2 has one of the highest fractions of landable terrain.

env.water_vapor_note: No atmosphere; Nobile crater interior is a major PSR; NR2 site 204 has an accessible PSR <110 K.
env.uv_note: Unfiltered solar UV; sun max ~7 deg elevation.
env.terrain: Crater rim highlands; NR2 ~57 km2 (14%) landable.
env.dust: Fine, charged highland regolith.

name: Haworth

env.water_vapor_note: No atmosphere; adjacent Haworth PSR and nearby Cabeus (LCROSS detected ~5.6 wt% water in ejecta).
env.uv_note: Unfiltered solar UV; sun max ~4.8 deg elevation.
env.terrain: Inter-crater highlands, ~77 km2 landable (8.7%).
env.dust: Fine, charged highland regolith.

env.water_vapor_note: No atmosphere; accessible PSRs <110 K at sites SP01/02/10/11.
env.uv_note: Unfiltered solar UV; sun max ~4.3 deg elevation.
env.terrain: Plain; ~77 km2 landable (19.3%, highest fraction).
env.dust: Fine, charged highland regolith.

name: Shiv Shakti Point (Chandrayaan-3)
summary: Chandrayaan-3 Vikram landing site (23 Aug 2023), first in-situ high-latitude regolith temperature profile (ChaSTE): 355 K peak on a 6 deg sun-facing slope vs ~330 K expected, showing metre-scale topography controls polar temperatures and that poleward slopes >14 deg could hold near-surface ice.

env.water_vapor_note: No atmosphere. ChaSTE: top ~10 cm shows ~55-85 K gradient during day; modelled night-time surface converges to ~105 K. Ice possible only on poleward slopes >14 deg (top 20 cm) per model.
env.uv_note: Unfiltered solar UV; sun reaches ~22 deg elevation.
env.terrain: Highland plains near Manzinus/Boguslawsky; lander on ~6 deg sunward local slope. APXS shows ferroan-anorthosite-like composition.
env.dust: Fine regolith; low thermal conductivity measured by ChaSTE.

sources.label: Durga Prasad et al. 2025 Commun. Earth Environ.: ChaSTE 355 K peak, ~105 K night
ISRO: ChaSTE in-situ measurement press release
Landing coordinates 69.373S 32.319E
Vadawale et al. 2024 Nature APXS

name: Mare Tranquillitatis Pit (lava-tube skylight)
summary: ~100 m-wide, ~100 m-deep collapse pit with an overhang; Mini-RF radar (Carrer et al. 2024) indicates an accessible subsurface cave conduit. Shaded areas under the overhang sit near a stable ~17 C, offering natural thermal, radiation and micrometeorite shielding for a habitat.

env.water_vapor_note: No atmosphere. Mean value is the near-isothermal ~290 K under the overhang/cave (varies <1 C); min/max are the open pit floor (~230 K night, ~415 K noon modelled). Surrounding mare surface: ~127 C day, ~-173 C night.
env.uv_note: Open surface: full unfiltered solar UV; overhang/cave interior: no direct UV.
env.terrain: Flat mare plains around a ~100 m vertical-walled pit with ~20+ m overhang; floor boulder-strewn.
env.dust: Mare regolith; cave interior expected to be sheltered from micrometeorite gardening.

sources.label: NASA 2022: LRO finds lunar pits ~17 C
Horvath et al. 2022 GRL: pit/cave thermal environment (290 K, floor ~415 K)
Carrer et al. 2024 Nature Astronomy: radar evidence of cave conduit
Pit coordinates

name: Marius Hills Pit
summary: ~65 x 90 m, ~34 m-deep skylight in the Marius Hills volcanic complex (Oceanus Procellarum), aligned with a sinuous rille; prime candidate lava-tube entrance (GRAIL gravity also suggests large voids).

env.water_vapor_note: No atmosphere. Mean = modelled cave/overhang temperature (~290 K); min/max = modelled open pit floor; surrounding surface ~127 C / -173 C.
env.uv_note: Open surface: full unfiltered solar UV; interior shielded.
env.terrain: Volcanic domes and cones on mare plains; pit along a rille.
env.dust: Mare regolith.

sources.label: NASA 2022: LRO finds lunar pits ~17 C (Marius Hills pit dims)
Wagner & Robinson 2022 JGR: Lunar pit morphology
Haruyama et al. 2009 GRL: Marius Hills hole discovery

name: Hadley–Apennine (Apollo 15, Hadley Rille)
summary: Apollo 15 landing site: mare basalt plain at the foot of the Apennine Mountains beside Hadley Rille (a collapsed lava channel/tube). Equatorial reference with measured heat-flow surface temperatures.

env.water_vapor_note: No atmosphere; no ice (equatorial, ~14-day lunar day).
env.uv_note: Full unfiltered solar UV including UVC.
env.terrain: Mare basalt plain; Hadley Rille ~1.5 km wide, ~300 m deep; Apennine massifs rise ~4-5 km.
env.dust: Mare regolith (Apollo 15 crews reported pervasive dust adhesion).

sources.label: NASA Apollo 15 mission

name: Jezero Crater (Perseverance)
summary: Ancient crater lake with a preserved delta; Perseverance is caching samples for Mars Sample Return. MEDA provides full weather record.

env.water_vapor_note: MEDA RH up to ~29% at night; column ~5-15 pr-um seasonally.
env.uv_note: No ozone shield: UVC (200-280 nm) reaches the surface; DNA-weighted dose up to ~3 orders of magnitude above Earth's (Cockell et al. 2000). MEDA RDS measures UV.
env.terrain: Crater floor, delta fan, rocky plains; thermal inertia 180-605 SI (MEDA).
env.dust: Dust optical depth 0.3-0.6 in clear season; frequent dust devils.

sources.label: Rodriguez-Manfredi et al. 2023 Nat. Geosci.: MEDA first 250 sols (650-761 Pa)

name: Gale Crater (Curiosity)
summary: Layered sedimentary record (Mount Sharp) of a long-lived lake system; REMS and RAD provide the reference Mars surface weather and radiation dataset.

env.water_vapor_note: Very dry; REMS RH near 0 by day, up to ~70% at night in winter; column ~5-10 pr-um.
env.uv_note: REMS UV sensor: strong UVC/UVB at surface modulated by dust; DNA-weighted far above Earth.
env.terrain: Crater floor plains (Aeolis Palus) rising onto Mount Sharp; dunes (Bagnold).
env.dust: Moderate dust; seasonal opacity ~0.3-1.5; global dust storm 2018.

sources.label: Hassler et al. 2014 Science: RAD 0.64 mSv/day

name: Arcadia Planitia (mid-latitude ground ice)
summary: Low-elevation northern plain with widespread shallow (<1 m) and decametre-thick excess water ice mapped by SWIM; the leading candidate region for a human landing that relies on ice ISRU.

env.water_vapor_note: Column ~10-30 pr-um (northern summer maximum); seasonal water/CO2 frost possible in winter.
env.uv_note: Unshielded UVC; somewhat lower than equator due to latitude.
env.terrain: Very flat plains, polygonal/patterned ground, terraced and expanded craters, ice-exposing scarps nearby.
env.dust: Moderate dust cover.

sources.label: SWIM project (PSI/NASA)

name: Utopia Planitia (Zhurong)
summary: Southern Utopia Planitia landing site of CNSA's Zhurong rover; possible ancient ocean-shoreline and buried water-related layers (RoPeR radar); hydrated duricrust observed.

env.water_vapor_note: Column ~10-20 pr-um; Zhurong MCS measured pressure 677.7-848.3 Pa and ~60 K day-night air temperature swing (average air ~218-268 K).
env.uv_note: Unshielded UVC.
env.terrain: Flat plains with troughs, cones, transverse aeolian ridges.
env.dust: Moderate dust; dust accumulation ended Zhurong's operations (2022).

name: Deuteronilus Mensae (debris-covered glaciers)
summary: Fretted terrain with lobate debris aprons and lineated valley fill confirmed by SHARAD as nearly pure glacial ice under a thin debris cover; proposed in NASA's 2015 Human Landing Site / Exploration Zone workshop.
missions: NASA Human Landing Sites EZ workshop (2015)

env.water_vapor_note: Column ~10-30 pr-um seasonally; winter CO2/H2O frost.
env.uv_note: Unshielded UVC; lower annual dose at 44N.
env.terrain: Mesas and buttes on the dichotomy boundary with debris aprons/glaciers several hundred m thick.
env.dust: Debris/dust mantle over ice, typically <1-10 m.

sources.label: Plaut et al. 2009 GRL: radar evidence for ice in lobate debris aprons

name: Meridiani Planum (Opportunity)
summary: Opportunity's site: hematite concretions ('blueberries') and jarosite-bearing sulfate sandstones recording acidic groundwater/evaporitic playas; equatorial, flat, safe for landing.

env.water_vapor_note: Column ~5-15 pr-um; no in-situ pressure sensor (value from Mars Climate Database for ~-1.4 km elevation).
env.uv_note: Unshielded UVC at equator.
env.terrain: Flat plains with basaltic sand ripples, small craters (Eagle, Endurance, Victoria) and Endeavour crater rim.
env.dust: Dark low-dust surface; 2018 global dust storm ended the mission.

sources.label: NASA MER Opportunity mission
Squyres et al. 2004 Science: in situ evidence for acidic, aqueous environment
Mars Climate Database (LMD)

name: Hellas Planitia floor
summary: Floor of the ~2,300 km Hellas impact basin, ~7 km below datum: the highest surface pressure on Mars (~1.1-1.2 kPa, well above water's triple point), giving the most radiation shielding and best EDL drag, but frequent dust storms and seasonal CO2 frost.

env.water_vapor_note: Column ~10-20 pr-um; pressure above triple point allows transient liquid/brine stability in models; seasonal frost in southern winter.
env.uv_note: Thicker column (~1.7x Gale) and dust reduce surface UVC somewhat.
env.terrain: Smooth to honeycomb-textured basin floor plains; dust-storm source region.
env.dust: High; major source of regional/global dust storms.

sources.label: Mars Climate Database (LMD) surface pressure
Hassler et al. 2014 RAD baseline (scaled by column mass)

name: Tharsis lava plains (Arsia Mons flank)
summary: Young Amazonian basaltic lava flows of the Tharsis rise southwest of Arsia Mons; analog target for basaltic volcanism, lava tubes/skylights (Arsia 'seven sisters' pits). High elevation means thin air, more radiation and very dusty, low-thermal-inertia surface.

env.water_vapor_note: Thin column (~3-6 pr-um) at high elevation; afternoon orographic water-ice clouds over the Tharsis volcanoes (aphelion season).
env.uv_note: Thinner atmosphere -> higher UVC dose than lowlands.
env.terrain: Lobate lava flows, collapse pits and sinuous channels; thick dust mantle.
env.dust: Very high dust cover (low thermal inertia region).

sources.label: Cushing et al. 2007 GRL: candidate cave skylights on Arsia Mons
Mars Climate Database (LMD)

name: Valles Marineris (Melas/Candor Chasma)
summary: Central Valles Marineris troughs with kilometre-thick layered sulfate deposits and possible recurring slope lineae; deep floors give higher pressure; spectacular canyon geology for a science base.
missions: Orbital only (MRO CRISM/HiRISE, MEX OMEGA); former MSL/M2020 candidate (Melas)

env.water_vapor_note: Column ~10 pr-um; TGO/FREND reported a hydrogen-rich (possible ice/hydrated mineral) region in Candor Chaos.
env.uv_note: Unshielded UVC; canyon walls shade parts of the floor.
env.terrain: Canyon floors 3-5 km below datum, walls up to 7-8 km high, landslides and interior layered deposits.
env.dust: Moderate.

sources.label: Mitrofanov et al. 2022 Icarus: TGO FREND hydrogen in Candor Chaos
Mars Climate Database (LMD)

name: Phoenix Landing Site (Green Valley, Vastitas Borealis)
summary: Arctic plain where Phoenix excavated water ice only ~3-18 cm below the surface and found perchlorate (~0.6 wt%) and carbonate in alkaline soil; observed snowfall from clouds.

env.water_vapor_note: Highest near-surface vapor of any lander site in summer (~30-50 pr-um column); night frost, ground fog and snow virga observed by LIDAR.
env.uv_note: Lower sun angle and longer path reduce peak UV, but no ozone shield.
env.terrain: Polygonal patterned ground (2-5 m polygons) over ice-cemented soil.
env.dust: Low-moderate; CO2 frost buries site in winter (lander killed by ice loading).
